question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

In the nick of time
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only just in time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in the nick of time" means at the very last moment before it is too late; only just in time. (ऐन मौके पर / ठीक समय पर)

◦ Example: The fireman reached the burning house in the nick of time and saved the child.

• The sense of the idiom is that of a narrow escape — something happens just before the deadline or disaster.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Frequently" means often/repeatedly — it expresses frequency, not timing.

• Option 3 "Every time" means on each occasion — again frequency, not a last-minute rescue.

• Option 4 "Meantime" means the period in between two events ("in the meantime") — unrelated to punctuality.

NOTE

• Related time idioms often asked in SSC: "against the clock" (in a hurry to finish before a deadline), "at the eleventh hour" (at the last possible moment), "high time" (the right time to act), "call it a day" (to stop work for the day).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Pay attention to what's happening and make _______ adjustments based on your personal experience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. reasonable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reasonable" means sensible, fair and based on good judgement. "Make reasonable adjustments" is a natural and very common collocation — sensible changes made in the light of experience. (उचित / तर्कसंगत)

◦ Correct: Pay attention to what's happening and make reasonable adjustments based on your personal experience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "impartial" means unbiased/neutral — it describes judges and decisions, not adjustments made from personal experience (indeed "personal experience" is the opposite of impartial evidence).

• Option 2 "honest" means truthful — one does not "make honest adjustments".

• Option 3 "placid" means calm and peaceful (used for lakes, temperaments) — it cannot describe adjustments.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "adjustments": make/ making minor, slight, necessary, reasonable, seasonal adjustments. In SSC fill-in-the-blank questions, always test the option for collocation as well as meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(Many a opportunities came and went while) he laid wasted.
option_1: Many an opportunity came and went while
option_3: Many an opportunities came and gone while
option_4: Many opportunities come and went as
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Many an opportunity came and went while.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "Many a / Many an" is always followed by a singular countable noun and a singular verb, even though the meaning is plural.

◦ Structure: Many a/an + singular noun + singular verb.

◦ Correct: Many an opportunity came and went while he laid wasted.

• Since "opportunity" begins with a vowel sound, "many an" (not "many a") is used.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed segment "Many a opportunities" wrongly joins "many a" with a plural noun.

• Option 3 "Many an opportunities came and gone while" repeats the plural error and also uses "gone" (V3) where the past tense "went" is required after "came and".

• Option 4 "Many opportunities come and went as" mixes the present tense "come" with the past tense "went", which breaks tense parallelism.

NOTE

• Compare: "Many a student has passed" (singular verb) = "Many students have passed" (plural verb). Both are correct; the trap is mixing the two patterns.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

The participants responds to a series of statements at the dance competition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The participants responds.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is an error of subject–verb agreement. The subject "The participants" is plural, so it must take the plural verb "respond", not the singular "responds".

◦ Correct: The participants respond to a series of statements at the dance competition.

• Rule: a singular subject takes a verb with "-s/-es" in the simple present (He responds); a plural subject takes the base verb (They respond).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to a series of statements" is correct — "respond to" is the right preposition.

• Option 4 "at the dance competition" is correct — "at" is used for events and points/locations.

• Option 3 "No error" is wrong because a clear agreement error exists.

NOTE

• Watch the "a series of / a bunch of / a pack of" trap: the verb agrees with the head noun ("A series of lectures was organised"), not with the noun after "of".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(Neither of the political factions have had much) interest in environmental intent.
option_2: Neither of the political factions have had any
option_3: Neither of the political faction has have much
option_4: Neither of the political factions has had much
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Neither of the political factions has had much.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Neither of + plural noun" is treated as singular, so it takes a singular verb: "Neither of the factions has", not "have".

◦ Correct: Neither of the political factions has had much interest in environmental intent.

• Similarly, "Either of / Each of / Neither of / None of (formal) / One of" + plural noun → singular verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No substitution required" retains the plural verb "have had", which violates the rule.

• Option 2 also keeps "have had" and additionally changes "much" to "any" unnecessarily.

• Option 3 "has have much" is a double-verb construction and is grammatically impossible; it also wrongly uses the singular "faction" after "neither of the".

NOTE

• Remember the pair: "Neither ... nor" takes a verb agreeing with the nearer subject (Neither the boys nor the teacher is present), whereas "Neither of" is always singular.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Lumber has many _______ beyond home building.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. uses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Uses" (plural of the noun "use") means the various purposes for which something can be employed. Lumber (sawn timber) has many uses apart from house construction — furniture, paper, packing crates, etc. (उपयोग)

◦ Correct: Lumber has many uses beyond home building.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "trunks" means the main stems of trees (or large boxes) — lumber is made from trunks; it does not "have trunks".

• Option 2 "loses" is a verb ("he loses"), not a noun, so it cannot follow "many"; the noun is "losses".

• Option 3 "pluses" means advantages/positive points — possible in casual speech but it does not fit "beyond home building", which clearly refers to additional applications.

NOTE

• Vocabulary: lumber/timber = wood prepared for building; log = an unsawn piece of trunk; plywood = layered wood board. Watch the spelling pair lose (verb, to misplace) and loose (adjective, not tight).

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

Don't start to think we've (won this game certainly), gentlemen.
option_4: got this game in the bag
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. got this game in the bag.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(to have something) in the bag" means to be certain of winning or achieving something; as good as won. It exactly replaces "won this game certainly". (जीत निश्चित होना)

◦ Correct: Don't start to think we've got this game in the bag, gentlemen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "swallowed the bitter truth" means accepted an unpleasant fact — the opposite mood of confident victory.

• Option 2 "held our horses" means waited patiently / slowed down — it does not convey certain victory.

• Option 3 "have skin in the game" means to have a personal stake or risk invested in something — not the same as being sure of winning.

NOTE

• Other "victory/confidence" idioms for SSC: "a walkover" (an easy win), "carry the day" (to win), "count your chickens before they hatch" (to assume success too early), "a done deal" (already settled).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

He is (frank) about what he sees as the shortcomings of his great predecessors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. evasive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Frank" means open, honest and direct in speech; saying plainly what one thinks. (स्पष्टवादी)

• Its antonym is "evasive", which means avoiding a direct answer; not straightforward. (टालमटोल करने वाला)

◦ Example: The minister gave an evasive reply instead of a frank admission.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "assisting" means helping — unrelated to plain speaking.

• Option 2 "cheerful" means happy — an antonym of "gloomy", not of "frank".

• Option 4 "fortunate" means lucky — an antonym of "unlucky".

NOTE

• Synonyms of frank: candid, forthright, blunt, outspoken, straightforward. Antonyms: evasive, secretive, guarded, insincere, devious.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Many people may not find the rewards _______ with the time and effort required.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. commensurate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Commensurate" means in proportion to; matching in size, quality or degree. The fixed collocation is "commensurate with". (अनुरूप / समानुपाती)

◦ Correct: Many people may not find the rewards commensurate with the time and effort required — i.e., the rewards may not match the effort put in.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "collude" is a verb meaning to conspire secretly ("collude with") — a verb cannot follow "find the rewards" here.

• Option 2 "coffer" is a noun meaning a strongbox or a store of money ("the state coffers").

• Option 4 "capable" (able to do something) takes "of", not "with", and cannot describe rewards.

NOTE

• Preposition pairs worth remembering: commensurate with, compatible with, comparable to/with, proportionate to, consistent with. Salary advertisements often say "salary commensurate with experience".

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Contribute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contribute" is the correct spelling. It means to give (money, help, ideas) towards a common purpose or result. (योगदान देना)

◦ Spelling key: CON + TRI + BUTE — one "r", one "b", and the ending "-bute".

◦ Example: Everyone was asked to contribute something to the relief fund.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Contrribute" wrongly doubles the r; "Contribbute" wrongly doubles the b; "Contribuet" wrongly reverses the last two letters of "-bute".

NOTE

• Word family: contribute (verb), contribution (noun), contributor (person), contributory (adjective, as in "contributory negligence"). Related "-tribute" words: tribute, attribute, distribute, retribution.

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: Microsoft announced plans to make bids to accquire Byte Dance.
option_2: The job of the artist is to make the revolution perceptible.
option_3: Except that it'll be rooted in awkard, funny and compelling reality.
option_4: She used the 14th Amendment to acheive equality.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The job of the artist is to make the revolution perceptible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 2 is correctly spelt. "Perceptible" means able to be seen or noticed. (बोधगम्य / दृष्टिगोचर)

◦ Spelling key: PER + CEP + TIBLE (it ends in "-ible", not "-able").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "accquire" is misspelt — the correct spelling is "acquire" (a-c-q-u-i-r-e), with a single "c".

• Option 3: "awkard" is misspelt — the correct spelling is "awkward" (with a "w" before the "a-r-d").

• Option 4: "acheive" is misspelt — the correct spelling is "achieve", which follows the rule "i before e except after c".

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt SSC words: acquire, achieve, awkward, occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, questionnaire, privilege, separate, definitely, receive.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Golden
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Shining.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Golden" means made of gold, or having the bright, gleaming, lustrous colour of gold. Its closest synonym among the options is "Shining" (bright and glowing). (सुनहरा / चमकीला)

◦ Example: The golden/shining dome of the temple glittered in the sunlight.

• Figuratively, "golden" also means excellent or precious — a "golden opportunity", the "golden age".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dull" (not bright, lacking shine) is an antonym.

• Option 2 "Gloomy" (dark and depressing) is also opposite in sense.

• Option 4 "Dark" (without light) is a clear antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of golden/shining: gleaming, glittering, radiant, lustrous, brilliant, resplendent. Antonyms: dull, dim, tarnished, murky.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The NCGG has been/ set up to assist in / bring about governance reforms through studies.
option_2: bring about governance reforms through studies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. bring about governance reforms through studies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "in" at the end of the previous segment must be followed by a gerund (V-ing), not the base form of the verb. So "assist in bring about" is wrong; it must be "assist in bringing about".

◦ Correct: The NCGG has been set up to assist in bringing about governance reforms through studies.

• Rule: Preposition + V-ing (gerund) — "good at swimming", "interested in reading", "insist on going", "assist in preparing".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "The NCGG has been" is correct (present perfect passive with "set up").

• Option 1 "set up to assist in" is correct in itself — the error appears only when the next word fails to take the "-ing" form.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because a definite error exists.

NOTE

• Beware of the trap word "to": in "look forward to, object to, be used to, with a view to", the "to" is a preposition, so it too takes V-ing ("I look forward to meeting you").

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I try to eat less meat and more vegetables.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "to eat less" is already correct.

◦ After "try", the to-infinitive is used, and an infinitive always takes the base form (V1) — "to eat".

◦ "Less" is the correct quantifier for uncountable nouns such as "meat" (less water, less sugar, less meat), whereas "fewer" is used with countable nouns (fewer books).

• Correct: I try to eat less meat and more vegetables.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to eats less" is wrong — no "-s" is added to a verb after "to".

• Option 2 "to eat lesser" is wrong — "lesser" means "smaller in importance/value" (the lesser evil) and is not used for quantity of food.

• Option 3 "to ate less" is wrong — the past tense "ate" cannot follow "to".

NOTE

• Quantity pairs: much/less/little with uncountables; many/fewer/few with countables; more works with both. "Amount of" (uncountable) vs "number of" (countable).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Eddie just panics/ when it gets close/ nearer the end.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. nearer the end.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "nearer the end" is faulty. The sentence already contains "close" in the previous segment, so putting the comparative "nearer" beside it creates a double/redundant comparison and leaves "close" without its required preposition "to".

◦ Correct: Eddie just panics when it gets close to the end. (or: ... when it gets nearer to the end.)

• Rule: the adjective "close" is followed by "to" — close to the door, close to the truth, close to the end.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Eddie just panics" is correct — singular subject with singular verb "panics".

• Option 3 "when it gets close" is correct in itself; the fault lies in the segment that follows it.

• Option 2 "No error" is wrong because the third segment is clearly defective.

NOTE

• Spelling point: verbs ending in "-ic" add "k" before "-ed/-ing": panic → panicked, panicking; picnic → picnicked; traffic → trafficking.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

The only one _______ shattered their monotony by his visits was Krishna.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. who ever.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a relative pronoun acting as the subject of the verb "shattered", and it refers to a person ("The only one ... was Krishna"). The subject form for a person is "who"; "ever" is added for emphasis.

◦ Correct: The only one who ever shattered their monotony by his visits was Krishna.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "whom ever" is wrong — "whom" is the object form; here the pronoun performs the action (it is followed directly by the verb "shattered").

• Options 2 "whatever" and 4 "which ever" are used for things, not for a person.

NOTE

• Quick test: if the pronoun is followed by a verb, use "who"; if it is followed by a subject + verb, use "whom". Compare: "the man who called me" / "the man whom I called".

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Irreverent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Respectful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Irreverent" means showing a lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously. (अनादरपूर्ण / अश्रद्धालु)

• Its antonym is "Respectful", meaning showing deference and regard. (आदरपूर्ण)

◦ Example: His irreverent jokes about the ceremony upset the elders, who expected a respectful silence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Restoration" is a noun meaning the act of restoring something to its former state — not an antonym.

• Option 3 "Dormant" means inactive or sleeping (a dormant volcano).

• Option 4 "Relevant" means closely connected with the matter in hand — it is the antonym of "irrelevant", a look-alike trap word.

NOTE

• Note the prefix "ir-" (a form of "in-" used before "r") meaning "not": irreverent, irrelevant, irregular, irresponsible, irrational, irresistible.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

One who hates or discriminates against women.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Misogynist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Misogynist" is a person who hates, dislikes or is strongly prejudiced against women. (स्त्री-द्वेषी)

◦ Word roots: Greek miso- = hatred + gyne = woman.

◦ Example: The novel exposes the misogynist attitudes of its era.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Pessimist" — one who always expects the worst.

• Option 3 "Feminist" — one who supports equal rights for women (the near-opposite of a misogynist).

• Option 4 "Atheist" — one who does not believe in the existence of God.

NOTE

• Related "miso-" words: misandrist (one who hates men), misanthrope (one who hates mankind), misogamist (one who hates marriage). Other useful one-word substitutes: misogyny (the hatred itself), philanthropist (a lover of mankind).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A violent wind that has a circular movement
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Hurricane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Hurricane" is a violent storm with a strong, circular (rotating) wind system, formed over warm tropical oceans. (चक्रवाती तूफ़ान)

◦ Example: The hurricane uprooted trees and flattened houses along the coast.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Drought" — a long period of abnormally low rainfall / water scarcity.

• Option 2 "Deluge" — a great flood or a very heavy downpour of rain.

• Option 3 "Tsunami" — a series of enormous sea waves caused by an undersea earthquake or volcanic eruption, not by wind.

NOTE

• Static-GK link: the same rotating tropical storm is called a hurricane in the Atlantic and eastern Pacific, a typhoon in the north-western Pacific, and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean region. A small violent land whirlwind is a tornado.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

I am parched, dehydrated to the point of pain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Drained.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dehydrated" means having lost water or moisture; dried out. Its closest synonym here is "Drained", meaning emptied of liquid / having the moisture removed. (निर्जलित / सूखा हुआ)

◦ The context word "parched" (extremely dry, very thirsty) confirms this sense of severe loss of water.

◦ Example: After hours in the sun the trekkers were completely dehydrated/drained.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Braced" means prepared or steadied oneself for something difficult.

• Option 2 "Moistened" (made slightly wet) is a clear antonym of dehydrated.

• Option 4 "Washed" means cleaned with water — it involves adding water, not losing it.

NOTE

• Synonyms of dehydrated: parched, desiccated, arid, drained, dried up. Antonyms: hydrated, moistened, saturated, drenched. Prefix "de-" = removal (dehydrate, defrost, deforest, devalue).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The figure of Arthur first appeared in Welsh poetry in the (1) ______ sixth and early seventh centuries, a hero who was (2) ______ lead the Britons in battle against Saxon invaders. But it wasn't (3) _______ the 12th century that he was first tied to this dramatic headland, known as Tintagel. The timeless popularity of the Arthur legend has overshadowed a central, unresolved (4) _______: Was there really a King Arthur, or at least a historical prototype upon whom Geoffrey's hero is (5) ______?

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. late.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is balanced against the words "and early seventh centuries" later in the same phrase. The natural pairing is "the late sixth and early seventh centuries" — i.e., the closing part of the 6th century and the opening part of the 7th.

◦ Correct: The figure of Arthur first appeared in Welsh poetry in the late sixth and early seventh centuries ...

• "Late" before a period of time means "towards the end of" (the late 1990s, the late Middle Ages) and is the direct opposite of "early".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "least" is the superlative of "little" and makes no sense with a century.

• Option 3 "latest" means "most recent" — it cannot describe a century in the distant past.

• Option 4 "latter" means "the second of two things already mentioned" and needs a prior pair to refer back to.

NOTE

• Contrast pairs used with periods: early / late, the turn of the century, mid- (the mid-nineteenth century). Note "later" (afterwards) versus "latter" (the second of two).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The figure of Arthur first appeared in Welsh poetry in the (1) ______ sixth and early seventh centuries, a hero who was (2) ______ lead the Britons in battle against Saxon invaders. But it wasn't (3) _______ the 12th century that he was first tied to this dramatic headland, known as Tintagel. The timeless popularity of the Arthur legend has overshadowed a central, unresolved (4) _______: Was there really a King Arthur, or at least a historical prototype upon whom Geoffrey's hero is (5) ______?

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. said to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passive structure "be said to + V1" means it is reported/believed that somebody does something. Since Arthur is a legendary figure whose deeds are only reported, this is exactly the sense required.

◦ Correct: ... a hero who was said to lead the Britons in battle against Saxon invaders.

◦ Structure: Subject + is/was said to + base verb — "He is said to be very rich."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "tamed to" (made docile) is meaningless with "lead the Britons".

• Option 3 "brought to" would need an object ("brought to justice") and does not fit before a base verb.

• Option 4 "told" is wrong because "was told lead" is ungrammatical — it would need "was told to lead", which also changes the meaning to receiving an order.

NOTE

• Similar reporting structures: "is believed to", "is supposed to", "is known to", "is thought to", "is reputed to". They are common in news and historical writing.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The figure of Arthur first appeared in Welsh poetry in the (1) ______ sixth and early seventh centuries, a hero who was (2) ______ lead the Britons in battle against Saxon invaders. But it wasn't (3) _______ the 12th century that he was first tied to this dramatic headland, known as Tintagel. The timeless popularity of the Arthur legend has overshadowed a central, unresolved (4) _______: Was there really a King Arthur, or at least a historical prototype upon whom Geoffrey's hero is (5) ______?

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. until.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed emphatic pattern is "It wasn't until + time + that + clause", meaning not before that time did the event happen.

◦ Correct: But it wasn't until the 12th century that he was first tied to this dramatic headland, known as Tintagel.

◦ Sense: only in the 12th century was Arthur first linked to Tintagel — not earlier.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "none" is a pronoun and cannot be followed by "the 12th century that ...".

• Option 2 "beyond" means "on the far side of / later than" and destroys the intended "not before" meaning.

• Option 4 "unless" means "if not" and introduces a condition, not a point of time.

NOTE

• Related cleft structures for emphasis: "It was only in 1947 that India became independent", "Not until the results came out did he relax" (note the inversion after a negative opening).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The figure of Arthur first appeared in Welsh poetry in the (1) ______ sixth and early seventh centuries, a hero who was (2) ______ lead the Britons in battle against Saxon invaders. But it wasn't (3) _______ the 12th century that he was first tied to this dramatic headland, known as Tintagel. The timeless popularity of the Arthur legend has overshadowed a central, unresolved (4) _______: Was there really a King Arthur, or at least a historical prototype upon whom Geoffrey's hero is (5) ______?

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. question.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The colon after the blank is followed by an actual interrogative sentence — "Was there really a King Arthur ...?" So the noun before the colon must be "question".

◦ Correct: ... has overshadowed a central, unresolved question: Was there really a King Arthur ...?

• The adjective "unresolved" also collocates naturally with "question", "issue" and "dispute".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "establishment" means an organisation or the act of setting something up.

• Option 2 "commotion" means noisy confusion or disturbance.

• Option 3 "mess" means an untidy or difficult state of affairs — too informal and not something that a colon-introduced question can explain.

NOTE

• Punctuation point: a colon (:) introduces an explanation, a list or, as here, the exact content of what has just been named. Collocations: an open/vexed/burning/unresolved question.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The figure of Arthur first appeared in Welsh poetry in the (1) ______ sixth and early seventh centuries, a hero who was (2) ______ lead the Britons in battle against Saxon invaders. But it wasn't (3) _______ the 12th century that he was first tied to this dramatic headland, known as Tintagel. The timeless popularity of the Arthur legend has overshadowed a central, unresolved (4) _______: Was there really a King Arthur, or at least a historical prototype upon whom Geoffrey's hero is (5) ______?

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. based.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence asks whether there was a real person "upon whom Geoffrey's hero is ...". The idiomatic phrase is "to be based upon/on somebody or something", meaning to be modelled on / derived from.

◦ Correct: ... or at least a historical prototype upon whom Geoffrey's hero is based?

◦ Example: The film is based on a true story.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "caged" (shut in a cage) makes no sense with "upon whom".

• Option 3 "hanged" refers to execution by hanging and does not take "upon whom".

• Option 4 "found" would require "in whom"/"by whom" and would not convey the idea of a model or prototype.

NOTE

• Note the verb pair: "hanged" is used only for execution (the convict was hanged), while "hung" is used for objects (the picture was hung). Collocation: "based on/upon", "modelled on", "drawn from".

question: Rabindranath Tagore started Santiniketan institute in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1901.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rabindranath Tagore founded his experimental school at Santiniketan (in Birbhum district, West Bengal) in 1901, beginning with only a handful of students in an open-air, nature-centred setting. (शांतिनिकेतन — 1901)

• The school was named Patha Bhavana and later grew into the university Visva-Bharati, which Tagore established in 1921; it became a Central University in 1951.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali, becoming the first non-European Nobel laureate in literature.

• He wrote India's national anthem "Jana Gana Mana" and Bangladesh's "Amar Sonar Bangla"; he renounced his knighthood after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919).

NOTE

• Santiniketan was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2023. Tagore's educational philosophy stressed learning in the open air, closeness to nature and the fusion of Indian and Western traditions.

question: Lomas Rishi cave is situated in which of the following Hills?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barabar Hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Lomas Rishi cave is situated in the Barabar Hills of the Jehanabad district of Bihar, about 24 km north of Gaya. (लोमस ऋषि गुफा — बराबर पहाड़ियाँ, बिहार)

• The Barabar caves are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Most of these caves were dedicated by Emperor Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha Maurya to the Ajivika sect.

• The Lomas Rishi cave is famous for its chaitya-arch doorway carved to imitate wooden construction, and for the mirror-like Mauryan polish on its interior walls.

NOTE

• The Barabar group (four caves) and the nearby Nagarjuni Hills (three caves) together represent the earliest phase of Indian rock-cut architecture, which later flowered at Ajanta, Ellora, Karle and Bhaja.

question: Archana wishes to contest for Lok Sabha elections in India. What is the maximum limit of constituencies that can she contest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Two.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Section 33(7) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate may contest an election from a maximum of two constituencies. (अधिकतम दो निर्वाचन क्षेत्र)

• If the candidate wins from both seats, Section 70 requires the person to resign one seat within 14 days, and a by-election is then held for the vacated seat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Before the 1996 amendment, there was no such cap and a person could contest from any number of seats.

• Basic qualifications for the Lok Sabha (Article 84): the person must be a citizen of India, at least 25 years of age, and must fulfil other qualifications prescribed by Parliament.

NOTE

• The Election Commission of India (Article 324) conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President. It has recommended reducing the limit to a single constituency.

question: Nahid Siddiqui was awarded Milapfest's Lifetime Achievement Award in October 2017. She is recognized for which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nahid Siddiqui is a celebrated exponent of the Kathak dance form. She received Milapfest's Lifetime Achievement Award in October 2017 for her contribution to Kathak. (कथक — नाहिद सिद्दीकी)

• Milapfest is a leading Indian arts development organisation based in the United Kingdom.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); the name comes from "Katha" (story) and "Kathakar" (storyteller).

• Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh; it is marked by rapid chakkars (spins), intricate tatkar (footwork) and expressive abhinaya.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: What chemical element does "Mn" stand for in the science periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manganese.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The symbol "Mn" in the periodic table stands for Manganese, a hard, brittle, silvery-grey transition metal with atomic number 25. (मैंगनीज़ — Mn)

• Manganese is essential in steel-making (it removes oxygen and sulphur and adds hardness) and is used in dry cells and in the manufacture of ferro-manganese alloys.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other options have different symbols: Magnesium = Mg (atomic number 12), Mendelevium = Md (101) and Molybdenum = Mo (42).

• India's chief manganese-producing states include Odisha, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; the main ore is pyrolusite (MnO₂).

NOTE

• Frequently confused symbols in SSC: Na (Sodium), K (Potassium), Fe (Iron), Cu (Copper), Ag (Silver), Au (Gold), Sn (Tin), Pb (Lead), Sb (Antimony), W (Tungsten).

question: The moon moves around the earth in about ______ days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 27.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Moon completes one revolution around the Earth in about 27.3 days — this is called the sidereal month. (लगभग 27 दिन)

• The Moon also takes about 27.3 days to rotate once on its axis. Because its rotation and revolution periods are equal (synchronous rotation), we always see the same face of the Moon from the Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The synodic month (new moon to new moon, i.e., the cycle of phases) is about 29.5 days, because the Earth also moves along its orbit in the meantime.

• The Moon is the Earth's only natural satellite; its light takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Earth, and its average distance is about 3,84,400 km.

NOTE

• The Moon has no atmosphere and its gravity is about 1/6th of the Earth's. Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to soft-land near the lunar south pole (23 August 2023), now observed as National Space Day.

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution provides for 'National commission for Scheduled Castes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 338.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 338 of the Constitution provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) — a constitutional body that investigates and monitors safeguards provided for the SCs. (अनुच्छेद 338 — राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति आयोग)

• The Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other members, appointed by the President.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 338A — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (created by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003, which split the earlier joint commission).

• Article 338B — National Commission for Backward Classes (given constitutional status by the 102nd Amendment Act, 2018).

• Article 337 deals with special provision for educational grants for the Anglo-Indian community; Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari script the official language of the Union; Article 344 provides for the Official Language Commission.

NOTE

• Other constitutional bodies: UPSC (Art. 315), Election Commission (Art. 324), Finance Commission (Art. 280), CAG (Art. 148) and the Attorney General (Art. 76).

question: The historical Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi and Amritsar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The stretch of highway known today as Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between Delhi and Amritsar — the north-western section of the historic Grand Trunk (GT) Road, formerly numbered NH-1. (शेरशाह सूरी मार्ग — दिल्ली से अमृतसर)

• It is named after Sher Shah Suri, the Sur ruler who rebuilt and extended this ancient highway in the 16th century.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The full Grand Trunk Road originally ran from Sonargaon (in present-day Bangladesh) through Delhi and Lahore up to Kabul (Afghanistan); Rudyard Kipling called it a "river of life" in Kim.

• Sher Shah planted shade trees, dug wells and built sarais (rest houses) along the road, and introduced the Rupiya (silver coin) and the Dak (postal) system.

NOTE

• Sher Shah Suri (1540–1545) defeated Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj/Bilgram (1540). His tomb is at Sasaram, Bihar. His revenue reforms later influenced Akbar's administration.

question: How many silver medals has won by India at Tokyo Olympics 2020 (played in 2021)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), India won 2 silver medals, out of a total of 7 medals — its best-ever Olympic haul. (2 रजत पदक)

◦ Mirabai Chanu — silver in weightlifting (49 kg women's).

◦ Ravi Kumar Dahiya — silver in wrestling (57 kg freestyle).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's full Tokyo tally: 1 gold (Neeraj Chopra, javelin throw — India's first-ever Olympic gold in athletics), 2 silver and 4 bronze.

• The bronze medals came from P. V. Sindhu (badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (boxing), Bajrang Punia (wrestling) and the men's hockey team, which won a medal after 41 years.

NOTE

• At the Paris Olympics 2024, India won 6 medals (1 silver, 5 bronze), with Neeraj Chopra taking silver in the javelin and Manu Bhaker winning two bronze medals in shooting.

question: Which famous female personality received the Padma Shri award for manipuri classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Elam Endira Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Elam Endira Devi, a distinguished exponent of the Manipuri classical dance form from Manipur, was honoured with the Padma Shri for her contribution to this art. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — एलम एंदिरा देवी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manipuri is the classical dance of Manipur, based largely on the Raas Leela of Radha and Krishna; it is gentle and rounded in movement, with the female dancer wearing the distinctive stiff barrel-shaped skirt called the Kumil/Potloi.

• Its drum-based male dance is the vigorous Pung Cholom, and the martial-style dance is Thang-Ta.

NOTE

• The Padma awards — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are announced on Republic Day and conferred by the President. The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of India.

question: Which king was shown on his coins as a Veena player?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samudragupta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gupta ruler Samudragupta (c. 335–380 CE) issued gold coins on which he is depicted playing the veena (lyre), showing his love of music and learning. (समुद्रगुप्त — वीणा वादक मुद्रा)

• Because of his extensive conquests, the historian V. A. Smith called him the "Napoleon of India".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• His achievements are recorded in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), composed by his court poet Harisena in Sanskrit.

• Samudragupta's coin types include the Archer, Battle-axe, Ashvamedha, Tiger-slayer and Lyrist (Veena) types. He performed the Ashvamedha yajna.

• He was the son of Chandragupta I and the father of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

NOTE

• The Gupta period (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India" for its achievements in art, literature (Kalidasa), mathematics (Aryabhata) and medicine, and for its purest gold coinage (dinaras).

question: Article 51A of the Indian constitution provides for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental Duties.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A, in Part IV-A of the Constitution, lays down the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India. (अनुच्छेद 51A — मूल कर्तव्य)

• They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Originally 10 in number, an 11th duty (providing education to children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts, just like the Directive Principles.

• Examples: to abide by the Constitution, to cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle, to protect the sovereignty of India, to protect the environment and to develop the scientific temper.

NOTE

• Related parts: Part III (Articles 12–35) — Fundamental Rights; Part IV (Articles 36–51) — Directive Principles; Part IV-A (Article 51A) — Fundamental Duties; Part V — the Union (Executive, Parliament, Judiciary).

question: Which of the following profession is a type of seasonal unemployment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Farmer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are unable to find work during certain seasons of the year. Farmers and agricultural labourers are its classic example, because farm work is available mainly at the times of sowing and harvesting and is scarce in between. (मौसमी बेरोज़गारी — किसान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other occupations subject to seasonal unemployment include ice-factory workers, sugar-mill (khandsari) workers, tourist guides and construction labourers in the monsoon.

• Disguised unemployment is also common in Indian agriculture — more people work on a farm than are actually needed, so the marginal productivity of the extra workers is nearly zero.

NOTE

• Types of unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, Structural, Cyclical, Frictional, Open, Educated and Technological. Government schemes such as MGNREGA (2005) guarantee 100 days of wage employment to rural households to reduce seasonal distress.

question: Limestone is a type of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedimentary rock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed mainly of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), formed from the accumulation and compaction of shells, corals and other marine remains on sea beds. (चूना पत्थर — अवसादी चट्टान)

• On metamorphism, limestone changes into marble.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sedimentary rocks are formed in layers (strata) by deposition and are the only rocks that contain fossils — examples: sandstone, shale, limestone, conglomerate.

• Igneous rocks form from the cooling of magma/lava (granite, basalt); metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks change under heat and pressure (marble, slate, gneiss, quartzite).

NOTE

• Uses of limestone: manufacture of cement, as a flux in blast furnaces for iron smelting, and in the making of lime. Karst topography, caves and stalactites are formed by the dissolution of limestone by rainwater.

question: Which country won the Women's Asia Cup 2022 of cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the Women's Asia Cup 2022 (T20 format), held in Sylhet, Bangladesh, by defeating Sri Lanka by 8 wickets in the final on 15 October 2022. (महिला एशिया कप 2022 — भारत)

• It was India's 7th title in the Women's Asia Cup, and the team was led by Harmanpreet Kaur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India has dominated the tournament, winning it in 2004, 2005, 2006, 2008, 2012, 2016 and 2022; Bangladesh won the 2018 edition.

• The Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC), founded in 1983.

NOTE

• Indian women's cricket landmarks: runners-up at the 2017 ODI World Cup and the 2020 T20 World Cup; gold at the Asian Games 2023; and the launch of the Women's Premier League (WPL) in 2023.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of "viviparous" animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bird.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Viviparous animals are those that give birth to live young ones rather than laying eggs. Dogs, cats and cows are all viviparous mammals. (जरायुज जंतु)

• Birds are oviparous — they lay eggs, which develop and hatch outside the mother's body. Hence a bird is NOT viviparous.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Oviparous animals (egg-laying): birds, most reptiles, amphibians, fishes and insects.

• Ovoviviparous animals retain the eggs inside the body until they hatch — for example, some sharks and snakes.

• Exceptional mammals: the platypus and echidna (spiny anteater) are egg-laying mammals (monotremes).

NOTE

• In viviparous animals the embryo develops inside the mother and receives nourishment through the placenta; the chances of survival of the young are therefore much higher than in oviparous animals.

question: The transformation of the larva into an adult through drastic change is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is metamorphosis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Metamorphosis" is the biological process in which a larva changes into an adult through a series of drastic structural changes. (कायांतरण / रूपांतरण)

◦ Examples: tadpole → frog; caterpillar → pupa → butterfly; maggot → housefly.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Complete metamorphosis has four stages — egg, larva, pupa and adult (butterfly, housefly, mosquito, beetle).

• Incomplete metamorphosis has three stages — egg, nymph and adult (cockroach, grasshopper, dragonfly).

• In frogs, metamorphosis is controlled by the hormone thyroxine secreted by the thyroid gland; iodine deficiency stops the tadpole from becoming a frog.

NOTE

• Option 1 "budding" is a mode of asexual reproduction (in Hydra and yeast), in which a bud grows on the parent body and detaches to become a new individual.

question: The Ahom Kingdom in India was located in the ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra valley.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ahom Kingdom was located in the Brahmaputra valley of present-day Assam. It was founded in 1228 CE by Sukapha, a Tai prince from Mong Mao (in present-day Myanmar/Yunnan). (अहोम साम्राज्य — ब्रह्मपुत्र घाटी, असम)

• The kingdom lasted for nearly 600 years, until it was annexed by the British after the Treaty of Yandabo (1826).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ahoms famously defeated the Mughal army under Ram Singh I at the Battle of Saraighat (1671), in which the Ahom general Lachit Borphukan led a brilliant naval defence on the Brahmaputra.

• Sukapha's ascent is commemorated every year on 24 November as Asom Divas (Sukapha Divas); Lachit Divas is observed on 24 November as well in honour of the general's valour.

• The Ahom system of forced labour was called Paik, and their chronicles were called Buranjis.

NOTE

• The Ahom Moidams (burial mounds) of Charaideo, Assam, were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024.

question: The Directive Principles of State Policy is included in which part of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IV.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are contained in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Indian Constitution. (भाग IV — राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व)

• They were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland and are non-justiciable — i.e., they cannot be enforced in a court of law, but Article 37 declares them "fundamental in the governance of the country".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part I (Articles 1–4) — the Union and its territory; Part II (Articles 5–11) — Citizenship; Part III (Articles 12–35) — Fundamental Rights.

• Important DPSPs: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code), Article 45 (early childhood care), Article 47 (prohibition of intoxicating drinks), Article 48A (protection of the environment) and Article 51 (promotion of international peace).

NOTE

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles as a "novel feature" of the Constitution, and Granville Austin called the DPSPs and Fundamental Rights together the "conscience of the Constitution".

question: An annual allowance for wear and tear of a capital good is known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is depreciation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Depreciation" is the annual allowance made for the wear and tear, obsolescence and normal ageing of a capital good (such as machinery or a building). It is also called consumption of fixed capital. (मूल्यह्रास)

◦ Formula link: Net Investment = Gross Investment – Depreciation; NNP = GNP – Depreciation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gross investment" is the total spending on new capital goods before deducting depreciation.

• Option 2 "devaluation" is a deliberate reduction in the external value of a country's currency by the government under a fixed exchange-rate system (India devalued the rupee in 1949, 1966 and 1991).

• Option 4 "disinvestment" is the sale of the government's equity stake in a public sector undertaking (handled by DIPAM).

NOTE

• Key national income identities: GDP (domestic output), GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad, NDP = GDP – depreciation, NNP at factor cost = National Income.

question: Indore gharana is one of the vocal gharanas of Indian classical music. It was founded by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Amir Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indore gharana of Hindustani classical vocal music was founded by Ustad Amir Khan (1912–1974). (इंदौर घराना — उस्ताद अमीर खाँ)

• His style is famous for the vilambit (very slow) khayal, a meditative merukhand approach to note patterns, and clear sargam and taranas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ustad Amir Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1971) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1967); he sang for films such as Baiju Bawra and Jhanak Jhanak Payal Baaje.

• Option 2 Doreswamy Iyengar was a veena maestro of Carnatic music; Option 3 Dr. L. Subramaniam is a celebrated violinist; Option 4 Ustad Bundu Khan was a sarangi player.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (the oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Rampur-Sahaswan, Bhendibazaar and Indore.

question: Guru Bipin Singh is associated with ________ dance form of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Bipin Singh (1918–2000) was the great guru of the Manipuri classical dance form, credited with systematising and popularising it — especially the solo form of Ras Leela — on the national stage. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — गुरु बिपिन सिंह)

• He trained the famous Jhaveri sisters (Nayana, Suverna, Ranjana and Darshana) and founded the Manipuri Nartanalaya.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manipuri dance is devotional in character, centred on the Radha–Krishna Ras Leela, with soft, flowing, rounded movements and the accompanying drum dance Pung Cholom.

• Option 2 "Kalbelia" is a folk dance of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan, inscribed in UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list (2010).

• Option 4 "Bachata" is a Latin American social dance from the Dominican Republic, not an Indian form.

NOTE

• Some noted dance gurus: Rukmini Devi Arundale (Bharatanatyam), Birju Maharaj (Kathak), Kelucharan Mohapatra (Odissi), Vempati Chinna Satyam (Kuchipudi) and Bipin Singh (Manipuri).

question: Diwali marks the day when lord Ram returned to Ayodhya after ______ years of exile after defeating king ravan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Diwali (Deepavali) commemorates the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile (vanvas) and his victory over Ravana, the king of Lanka. The people of Ayodhya lit rows of earthen lamps (deepa + avali = a row of lamps) to welcome him. (14 वर्ष का वनवास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Diwali falls on the Amavasya (new moon) of the Hindu month of Kartika, and the five-day festival includes Dhanteras, Naraka Chaturdashi, Lakshmi Puja, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj.

• For Jains, Diwali marks the nirvana of Lord Mahavira (527 BCE); for Sikhs it is Bandi Chhor Divas, marking the release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior fort.

NOTE

• The Ramayana was composed by Maharishi Valmiki; the Awadhi retelling Ramcharitmanas was written by Goswami Tulsidas. The Deepotsav of Ayodhya has repeatedly set Guinness World Records for the number of diyas lit.

question: As per the 2011 census of India, which Indian state has the lowest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among the states — 879 females per 1,000 males. (हरियाणा — सबसे कम लिंगानुपात)

• The national sex ratio in 2011 was 943 females per 1,000 males.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio among states (1,084), followed by Puducherry (1,037) among UTs; the lowest among all UTs was Daman and Diu (618).

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, the lowest since independence, with Haryana (834) again at the bottom.

NOTE

• The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched from Panipat, Haryana, on 22 January 2015 to address the declining child sex ratio. Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since independence; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

question: Shiv Dayal Saheb, a banker from Agra, founded the Radha Soami Satsang in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1861.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shiv Dayal Saheb (Soamiji Maharaj), a banker of Agra, founded the Radha Soami Satsang in 1861. (राधा स्वामी सत्संग — 1861, आगरा)

• The movement teaches devotion to a living guru (Sant Satguru), the practice of Surat Shabd Yoga (union of the soul with the divine sound current), a vegetarian diet and abstention from intoxicants.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Radha Soami faith cuts across caste and creed and does not insist on external ritual; its main centres include Soami Bagh and Dayalbagh (Agra) and Beas (Punjab).

• It is counted among the 19th-century socio-religious reform movements of India, alongside the Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828), the Prarthana Samaj (1867), the Arya Samaj (Dayanand Saraswati, 1875) and the Ramakrishna Mission (Swami Vivekananda, 1897).

NOTE

• Other reform bodies often asked in SSC: the Theosophical Society (1875, Blavatsky and Olcott), the Aligarh Movement (Sir Syed Ahmad Khan), the Satyashodhak Samaj (Jyotiba Phule, 1873) and the Deoband Movement (1866).
